'''Aitor Karanka de la Hoz''' (<small>Basque and </small>{{IPA|es|ajˈtoɾ kaˈɾaŋka}}; born 18 September 1973) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[central defender]], currently a [[Manager (association football)|manager]].

Save for a brief spell in the United States at age 32, he played solely in Spain for [[Athletic Bilbao]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], appearing in 275 [[La Liga]] matches over 13 seasons and winning six honours with the latter club.<ref name=First>{{cite news|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/alaves/marcos-primero-futbolistas-alaveses-partidos-primera-20250219171250-nt.html|title=De Marcos es el primero, ¿pero quiénes son los otros futbolistas alaveses con más partidos en Primera?|trans-title=De Marcos is the first, but who are the other Álava-born footballers with the most matches in ''Primera''?|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|first=Jon|last=Prada|language=es|date=19 February 2025|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref> He earned one [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], in 1995.

Karanka started working as a coach in the late 2000s, beginning as assistant manager at Real Madrid during [[José Mourinho]]'s tenure from 2010 to 2013.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2010/06/07/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1275916310.html|title=Butragueño: "Karanka representa los valores de la casa"|trans-title=Butragueño: "Karanka is what this place stands for"|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=7 June 2010|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/9219288/Cristiano-Ronaldo-is-the-best-in-the-world-says-Real-Madrid-assistant-coach-Aitor-Karanka-after-Barcelona-win.html|title=Cristiano Ronaldo is the best in the world, says Real Madrid assistant coach Aitor Karanka, after Barcelona win|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=22 April 2012|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/news/story/_/id/1237601/aitor-karanka-demanding-focus-from-real-madrid-agaist-betis|title=Karanka demanding focus from Real|publisher=[[ESPN]]|first=Miguel|last=Delaney|date=23 November 2012|access-date=27 February 2022}}</ref> He was appointed at [[EFL Championship]] club [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] in 2013, guiding them to promotion to the [[Premier League]] in 2016 before being dismissed the following year. He was subsequently in charge of [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in the Championship, before brief top-flight spells at [[Granada CF|Granada]] in Spain and [[Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in the [[Israeli Premier League]].

==Club career==
===Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid===
Born in [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]], [[Álava]], Karanka began his development with hometown club [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] and [[Athletic Bilbao Cantera|finished it]] with [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] neighbours [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/karanka-la-ilusion-que-se-ve-desde-fuera-esta-dentro|title=Karanka: "La ilusión que se ve desde fuera está dentro"|trans-title=Karanka: "The excitement one can see from the outside is on the inside"|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|language=es|date=4 August 2025|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref><ref name=First/> He made his senior debut with the [[Athletic Bilbao B|reserves of the latter]] in 1992, competing in the [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/athletic/aitor-karanka-explica-debut-athletic-marcha-real-20260122171250-nt.html|title=Aitor Karanka explica cómo fue su debut con el Athletic y su marcha al Real Madrid|trans-title=Aitor Karanka explains how his debut with Athletic Bilbao went and his move to Real Madrid|newspaper=El Correo|first1=Bruno|last=Vergara|language=es|date=22 January 2026|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref>

Karanka was promoted to the main squad by [[Jupp Heynckes]] in summer 1993 following the departure of [[Rafael Alkorta]].<ref name=First/> He made his [[La Liga]] debut on 7 November by playing 90 minutes in a 1–1 away draw against [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta de Vigo]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1993/11/07/pagina-19/1479540/pdf.html|title=Heynckes lleva a cabo la revolución que anunció|trans-title=Heynckes delivers promised revolution|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first1=Antonio|last1=Mínguez|first2=Eduardo|last2=Castañeda|language=es|date=7 November 1993|access-date=10 January 2014}}</ref> going on to feature in exactly 100 league matches in his three full seasons before joining the German [[Coach (sport)|coach]] at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in August 1997 (replacing Alkorta who had just rejoined Athletic Bilbao).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1997/08/13/deportes/871423202_850215.html|title=Karanka, defensa central del Athletic, acepta la oferta para fichar por el Madrid|trans-title=Karanka, Athletic central defender, accepts the offer to sign for Madrid|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Mábel|last=Galaz|language=es|date=13 August 1997|access-date=15 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com./EMD03/HEM/1997/08/14/MD19970814-021.pdf|title=Llegó el central|trans-title=Stopper has arrived|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Carlos E.|last=Carbajosa|language=es|date=14 August 1997|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref>

Karanka was used mostly as a backup by the capital-based team, but appeared in 33 [[UEFA Champions League]] matches for them<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/karanka-in-ec.html|title=Aitor Karanka de la Hoz – Matches in European Cups|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first=Emilio|last=Pla Díaz|access-date=28 October 2006}}</ref> including [[2000 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] of the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|1999–2000 edition]], a 3–0 win over against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/24/championsleague.sport1|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Valencia|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 May 2000|access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref> He missed the vast majority of the [[1998–99 La Liga|1998–99 campaign]] due to a heart condition.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/1998/marzo/04/deportes/karanka.html|title=Karanka y su corazón dicen hasta pronto|trans-title=Karanka and his heart say see you later|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Carlos E.|last=Carbajosa|language=es|date=4 March 1998|access-date=14 December 2010}}</ref>

===Athletic return, United States===
[[File:Karanka.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Karanka training with Athletic in December 2003]]
For [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03]], Karanka returned to Athletic Bilbao on a three-year contract with a €40&nbsp;million [[buyout clause]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com./EMD03/PUB/2002/05/29/EMD20020529008MDG.pdf|title=El mejor refuerzo|trans-title=The best addition|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Nika|last=Cuenca|language=es|date=29 May 2002|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref> He helped the ''Lions'' to [[2004–05 UEFA Cup|qualify]] for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] in his [[2003–04 La Liga|second year]] after finishing fifth in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://assets.laliga.com/assets/2019/12/17/originals/446f9acd8049c238c01312f5d91a14d3.pdf|title=Memoria de La Liga de Fútbol Profesional {{!}} Temporada 2003/2004 {{!}} Volumen I|trans-title=Memory of the Professional Football League {{!}} 2003/2004 season {{!}} Volume I|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=17 December 2019|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

In July 2006, Karanka signed for [[Colorado Rapids]] of [[Major League Soccer]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2006/07/03/specially-made-in-spain/|title=Specially made in Spain|newspaper=[[The Denver Post]]|first=Brian|last=Forbes|date=3 July 2006|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.philadelphiaunion.com/news/2011/07/real-madrid-got-real-test-union-says-kak%C3%A1|title=Real Madrid got real test from Union, says Kaká|publisher=Philadelphia Union|date=24 July 2011|access-date=11 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907094807/http://www.philadelphiaunion.com/news/2011/07/real-madrid-got-real-test-union-says-kak%C3%A1|archive-date=7 September 2012}}</ref> In his [[2006 Major League Soccer season|only season]], he helped his side to the [[Western Conference (MLS)|Western Conference]] play-off final, despite having his attempt saved by [[FC Dallas]]' [[Darío Sala]] in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] victory in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/rapids/ci_4569406|title=Shootout repeats history|newspaper=The Denver Post|first=Brian|last=Forbes|date=29 October 2006|access-date=17 May 2015}}</ref>

==International career==
Karanka's only appearance for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at senior level took place on 26 April 1995, in a 2–0 defeat of [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]] in [[Yerevan]] for the [[UEFA Euro 1996]] [[UEFA Euro 1996 qualifying|qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1995/04/27/pagina-4/1303698/pdf.html|title=Amavisca se estrena|trans-title=Amavisca gets his first|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Jesús|last=Gallego|language=es|date=27 April 1995|access-date=26 April 2013}}</ref> He added 14 for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21s]], being a member of the team that finished runners-up at the [[1996 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|1996 European Championship]] in a final lost to [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orgullobianconero.vavel.com/2013/06/18/italia-ya-gano-un-europeo-a-espana-en-el-1996/|title=Italia ya ganó un Europeo a España en el 1996|trans-title=Italy have already won European Championships against Spain in 1996|publisher=Orgullo Bianconero|language=es|date=18 June 2013|access-date=13 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113165559/http://www.orgullobianconero.vavel.com/2013/06/18/italia-ya-gano-un-europeo-a-espana-en-el-1996/|archive-date=13 November 2013}}</ref>

Karanka also represented [[Spain national under-23 football team|the nation]] in the [[1996 Summer Olympics]] in [[Atlanta]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/sport/real-aitor-karanka---part-6754039|title=The real Aitor Karanka – Part Two: Aitor and the golden generation|publisher=[[Teesside Live]]|first=Philip|last=Tallentire|date=27 February 2014|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/noticias/2021/07/22/el-athletic-y-los-jjoo/|title=El Athletic y los JJOO|trans-title=Athletic and the OG|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|language=es|date=22 July 2021|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref> playing four matches in a [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics|quarter-final exit]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1996/07/21/pagina-54/1334617/pdf.html#&mode=fullScreen|title=Mágico gol de Óscar|trans-title=Óscar wonder goal|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Cristina|last=Cubero|language=es|date=21 July 1996|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1996/07/23/pagina-54/1336584/pdf.html|title=Óscar, otra vez vital|trans-title=Óscar, crucial again|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Cristina|last=Cubero|language=es|date=23 July 1996|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1996/07/26/pagina-12/1313017/pdf.html|title=Argentina, en el camino|trans-title=Argentina, in the way|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Cristina|last=Cubero|language=es|date=26 July 1996|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1996/07/29/pagina-16/1484199/pdf.html|title=Cuartos gafes|trans-title=Jinxed last-eight|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Cristina|last=Cubero|language=es|date=29 July 1996|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
===Early career===
Having first worked in a development role with the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]], Karanka became head coach of the [[Spain national under-16 football team|Spain under-16 national team]] in August 2008.<ref name=Protege>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24927835|title=Aitor Karanka: Middlesbrough pin hopes on Jose Mourinho protege|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Joe|last=Townsend|date=14 November 2013|access-date=24 June 2025}}</ref> In June 2010, he was named assistant at Real Madrid by newly appointed manager [[José Mourinho]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2010/06/06/mas_futbol/1275805634_850215.html|title=Karanka será el segundo entrenador que pidió Mourinho|trans-title=Karanka will be the assistant coach requested by Mourinho|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Carmen|last=Colino|language=es|date=6 June 2010|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref> he had been recommended to the role by his former club teammates [[Luís Figo]], [[Predrag Mijatović]] and [[Clarence Seedorf]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/oct/17/aitor-karanka-middlesbough-basque-manager|title=Aitor Karanka is starting to make the difference for Middlesbrough|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Louise|last=Taylor|date=17 October 2014|access-date=24 June 2025}}</ref> During their tenure, the team won the [[2010–11 Copa del Rey]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/match_report/0,19764,11065_3365041,00.html|title=Madrid clinch Copa del Rey|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=20 April 2011|access-date=24 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110423012003/http://www.skysports.com/football/match_report/0%2C19764%2C11065_3365041%2C00.html|archive-date=23 April 2011}}</ref> the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12 national championship]] and the [[2012 Supercopa de España|2012 edition]] of the [[Supercopa de España]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/02052012/58/liga-real-madrid-win-liga-title-bilbao.html|title=Liga – Real Madrid win Liga title in Bilbao|publisher=[[Yahoo]]|date=May 2012|access-date=24 June 2025|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200522173227/http://uk.sports.yahoo.com/|archive-date=22 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330116297457/noticia/Noticia/Mourinho_is_the_only_coach_who_has_won_the_Super_Cup_in_four_different_European_countries.htm|title=Mourinho is the only coach who has won the Super Cup in four different European countries|publisher=Real Madrid CF|first=Alberto|last=Navarro|date=30 August 2012|access-date=24 June 2025|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120901221356/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330116297457/noticia/Noticia/Mourinho_is_the_only_coach_who_has_won_the_Super_Cup_in_four_different_European_countries.htm|archive-date=1 September 2012}}</ref>

In July 2013, Karanka left Real after the arrival of [[Carlo Ancelotti]], who brought his own coaching staff.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadridnews.com/aitor-karanka-and-real-madrid-part-ways/|title=Aitor Karanka and Real Madrid part ways|publisher=Real Madrid News|first=Paul|last=Collins|date=16 July 2013|access-date=4 August 2013}}</ref> Mourinho offered him the opportunity to follow him to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], but he declined his offer in order to fulfill his ambition to pursue his own venture in management.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/karanka-rejected-mourinho-and-chelsea|title=Karanka rejected Mourinho and Chelsea|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=6 December 2013|access-date=24 June 2025}}</ref><ref name=Protege/>

===Middlesbrough===
[[File:Ian Holloway Aitor Karanka December 2014.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Karanka on the sidelines ([[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]]'s [[Ian Holloway]] pictured right) in December 2014]]
On 13 November 2013, Karanka was appointed manager of [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], replacing [[Tony Mowbray]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24925713|title=Aitor Karanka: Middlesbrough name ex-Real Madrid man as boss|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 November 2013|access-date=13 November 2013}}</ref> His first match in charge ended in a 2–1 defeat away to [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] ten days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24969676|title=Leeds United 2–1 Middlesbrough|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 November 2013|access-date=23 November 2013}}</ref>

On 25 April 2015, in the penultimate game of [[2014–15 Football League Championship|the season]] at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], Karanka sent goalkeeper [[Dimitrios Konstantopoulos]] forward for an added-time corner kick with the score 3–3; with the goalkeeper out of position, the opponents scored a winner through [[Ross McCormack]], which sent [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] into the [[Premier League]] and jeopardised Middlesbrough's own chances of promotion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32470333|title=Aitor Karanka: Middlesbrough risk dents Premier League dream|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 April 2015|access-date=25 April 2015}}</ref> He did qualify his team to the [[2015 Football League Championship play-off final|play-off final]] after a 5–1 aggregate win over [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32636569|title=Middlesbrough 3–0 Brentford|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Matt|last=Newsum|date=15 May 2015|access-date=20 May 2015}}</ref> but they lost the decider 2–0 to [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32776552|title=Middlesbrough 0–2 Norwich|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=Shepka|date=25 May 2015|access-date=25 May 2015}}</ref>

Karanka signed a new four-year contract in August 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33825905|title=Aitor Karanka: Middlesbrough head coach signs new deal|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 August 2015|access-date=7 August 2015}}</ref> Boro were consistently in high positions during [[2015–16 Football League Championship|the campaign]], but on 11 March 2016 he unexpectedly left the training ground after an argument and considered his future at the [[Riverside Stadium]]. Responsibilities for the subsequent fixture against [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] were handed to his assistant [[Steve Agnew]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35793540|title=Aitor Karanka: Middlesbrough head coach considering future at Riverside|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2016|access-date=12 March 2016}}</ref> but the Spaniard returned to lead the team to the top division after a seven-year absence, as runners-up.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1098932/middlesbrough-promoted-to-the-premier-league/|title=Middlesbrough strike it rich with Premier League promotion|newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=7 May 2016|access-date=11 May 2016}}</ref>

In [[2016–17 Premier League|2016–17]], Karanka led his team to the [[2016–17 FA Cup|last eight]] of the [[FA Cup]], where they were eliminated by [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. He was sacked on 16 March 2017 with the team three points from safety and without a league win in the new year (while their defence was the fifth best in the division, their attack was the worst with just 19 goals from 27 matches, and he had disagreements with players, fans and the board).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39291081|title=Aitor Karanka: Middlesbrough sack manager after three and a half years|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 March 2017|access-date=16 March 2017}}</ref> Club and manager parted ways by mutual consent, as the latter believed he could take the team no further.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11680/10804567/middlesbrough-chairman-steve-gibson-says-tired-aitor-karanka-sacrificed-himself|title=Middlesbrough chairman Steve Gibson says tired Aitor Karanka 'sacrificed himself'|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=17 March 2017|access-date=17 March 2017}}</ref>

===Nottingham Forest===
On 8 January 2018, Karanka returned to the Championship after being appointed as manager of [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2018/january/nottingham-forest-sign-new-manager/|title=Nottingham Forest sign new manager|publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C.|date=8 January 2018|access-date=9 January 2018}}</ref> he replaced [[Gary Brazil]], who had been acting as [[caretaker manager|caretaker]] following the dismissal of [[Mark Warburton]], who had in turn left the side sitting 14th in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42528150|title=Mark Warburton: Nottingham Forest sack manager after nine months in charge|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 December 2017|access-date=1 January 2018}}</ref> He oversaw his first game five days later, a 1–0 defeat against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11688/11204735/nottingham-forest-0-1-aston-villa-scott-hogan-ruins-aitor-karankas-bow|title=Nottingham Forest 0–1 Aston Villa: Scott Hogan ruins Aitor Karanka's bow|publisher=Sky Sports|date=13 January 2018|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref> and on 7 April suffered a 2–0 loss at his former employers Middlesbrough.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11680/11319314/middlesbrough-2-0-nottingham-forest-aitor-karanka-beaten-on-riverside-return|title=Middlesbrough 2–0 Nottingham Forest: Aitor Karanka beaten on Riverside return|publisher=Sky Sports|date=7 April 2018|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref>

In summer 2018, Karanka signed [[João Carvalho (footballer, born 1997)|João Carvalho]] from [[S.L. Benfica]] for £13.2&nbsp;million, the club's most expensive transfer acquisition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/06/13/nottingham-forest-smash-transfer-record-signing-joao-carvalho/|title=Nottingham Forest to smash their transfer record with £13.2m signing of Benfica star Joao Carvalho|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|first=John|last=Percy|date=13 June 2018|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/en-us/agora/noticias/2017_2018/06/14/futebol-benfica-joao-carvalho-transferido-para-o-nottingham-forest|title=João Carvalho transferred to Nottingham Forest|publisher=S.L. Benfica|date=14 June 2018|access-date=29 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2018/june/forest-agree-double-signing/|title=Forest agree double signing|publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C.|date=14 June 2018|access-date=29 July 2020}}</ref> Forest began [[2018–19 EFL Championship|the season]] on a high note, going on a five-match undefeated run.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45229939|title=Nottingham Forest 2–2 Birmingham City|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 August 2018|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref> They continued their positive form up until December,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2018/december/match-report-forest-vs-ipswich-town/|title=Forest 2–0 Ipswich|publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C.|date=1 December 2018|access-date=29 July 2020}}</ref> where they only won one out of six matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/01/11/inside-story-aitor-karankas-downfall-nottingham-forest/|title=The inside story of Aitor Karanka's downfall at Nottingham Forest|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|first=John|last=Percy|date=11 January 2019|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref> 

Karanka left on 11 January 2019 after requesting to be released from his contract, with the team in seventh position four points behind the play-off places.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46822599|title=Aitor Karanka: Nottingham Forest manager leaves Championship club|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 January 2019|access-date=11 January 2019}}</ref> A key reason behind his departure was the breakdown in relationship between him and Forest's chief executive, Ioannis Vrentzos.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2565880/2021/05/06/nottingham-forest-chief-executive-vrentzos-considering-role-club/|title=Nottingham Forest chief executive Ioannis Vrentzos considering his role within the club|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|first=Daniel|last=Taylor|date=6 May 2021|access-date=6 May 2021}}</ref>

===Birmingham City===
On 31 July 2020, Karanka remained in the English second tier by becoming head coach of [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11694/12040127/aitor-karanka-appointed-birmingham-city-head-coach|title=Aitor Karanka appointed Birmingham City head coach|publisher=Sky Sports|date=31 July 2020|access-date=31 July 2020}}</ref> On 16 March 2021, he stepped down from his role after a run of three victories in 19 matches left the side just outside the [[2020–21 EFL Championship|relegation zone]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bcfc.com/news/articles/2021/club-statement-aitor-karanka/|title=Club statement: Aitor Karanka|publisher=Birmingham City F.C.|date=16 March 2021|access-date=16 March 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422044623/https://bcfc.com/news/articles/2021/club-statement-aitor-karanka/|archive-date=22 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/premier-league/2021/03/14/604e46eee2704eaeaa8b4590.html|title=Karanka and Birmingham part ways|newspaper=Marca|date=14 March 2021|access-date=16 March 2021}}</ref> and [[Lee Bowyer]] was announced as his successor shortly after.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11694/12246948/lee-bowyer-birmingham-city-appoint-former-charlton-boss-as-replacement-for-aitor-karanka|title=Lee Bowyer: Birmingham City appoint former Charlton boss as replacement for Aitor Karanka|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Lyall|last=Thomas|date=16 March 2021|access-date=16 March 2021}}</ref>

===Granada===
Following a 4–1 defeat at home to [[UD Levante|Levante]] on 17 April 2022, [[Granada CF|Granada]] dismissed interim [[Rubén Torrecilla]] and appointed Karanka as his replacement, tasked with using the remaining six matches to avoid relegation from the Spanish top flight.<ref name=GranadaIn>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2022/04/18/625dc2c646163f32678b4602.html|title=Granada announce Aitor Karanka as new head coach|newspaper=Marca|first=Jorge|last=Azcoytia|date=18 April 2022|access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref> He made his debut on 20 April, securing a goalless draw at reigning champions [[Atlético Madrid]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/atletico-madrid-granada-match-report-5743524-Apr2022/|title=Atletico Madrid fail to strengthen top-four bid after goalless draw|publisher=[[TheJournal.ie#The 42|The 42]]|date=20 April 2022|access-date=27 April 2022}}</ref> and won two of the fixtures, but a final-day draw against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] was not enough to [[2021–22 La Liga|secure safety]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-soccer-jorge-molina-spain-la-liga-c7765556d4375fa1dfee4676a5f248a6|title=Granada relegated in Spain after missed penalty|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|first=Tales|last=Azzoni|date=22 May 2022|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref>

Karanka was confirmed for the [[2022–23 Segunda División|next season]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20220607/1001819111/karanka-sigue-entrenador-granada.html|title=Karanka sigue como entrenador del Granada|trans-title=Karanka continues as Granada head coach|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Julio|last=Terrón|date=7 June 2022|access-date=13 June 2022}}</ref> but was relieved of his duties on 8 November 2022 after one win in five games.<ref name=GranadaOut>{{cite web|url=https://www.granadacf.es/noticia/comunicado-oficial-aitor-karanka|title=Comunicado oficial {{!}} Aitor Karanka|trans-title=Official announcement {{!}} Aitor Karanka|publisher=Granada CF|language=es|date=8 November 2022|accessdate=8 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/former-middlesbrough-manager-aitor-karanka-25473138|title=Former Middlesbrough manager Aitor Karanka sacked by Granada after seven months in the job|publisher=TeessideLive|first=Craig|last=Johns|date=9 November 2022|access-date=10 November 2022}}</ref>

===Maccabi Tel Aviv===
On 4 January 2023, Karanka agreed to an 18-month contract at [[Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in the [[Israeli Premier League]].<ref name=MTelAvivIn>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/futbol-internacional/2023/01/04/63b547f122601d5e418b4590.html|title=Karanka, nuevo entrenador del Maccabi Tel Aviv|trans-title=Karanka, new manager of Maccabi Tel Aviv|newspaper=Marca|first=Alberto|last=Rubio|language=es|date=4 January 2023|access-date=30 June 2023}}</ref> He left by mutual accord in June, having [[2022–23 Israeli Premier League|finished third in the league]] and reached the [[2022–23 Israel State Cup|semi-finals]] of the [[Israel State Cup|State Cup]].<ref name=MTelAvivOut>{{cite web|url=https://www.cope.es/deportes/futbol/futbol-internacional/noticias/aitor-karanka-continuara-como-entrenador-del-maccabi-tel-aviv-20230625_2781155|title=Aitor Karanka no continuará como entrenador del Maccabi Tel Aviv|trans-title=Aitor Karanka will not continue as manager of Maccabi Tel Aviv|publisher=[[Cadena COPE]]|language=es|date=25 June 2023|access-date=30 June 2023}}</ref>

==Other work==
In May 2021, Karanka organised an online coaching conference in association with the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]], under the name AK Coaches' World. The event focused on women's football, and participants included [[Iraia Iturregi]], [[Julen Lopetegui]], [[Mila Martínez]], [[Monchi]], [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] and [[Jorge Vilda]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2021/05/14/609e6b4746163f37798b4574.html|title=Women's football set to take centre stage at AK Coaches' World|newspaper=Marca|date=14 May 2021|access-date=11 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2021/05/14/609e74db268e3ed16e8b45d7.html|title=Aitor Karanka launches AK Coaches' World|newspaper=Marca|first1=Alberto|last1=Rubio|first2=Gregor|last2=Chappelle|date=14 May 2021|access-date=11 January 2022}}</ref>

Karanka was appointed [[sporting director]] at the Spanish Federation in July 2025, replacing [[Albert Luque]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/seleccion/karanka-nuevo-director-deportivo-de-la-seleccion-julen-guerrero-vuelve-a-la-sub-21-n/|title=Karanka será el nuevo director deportivo de la Selección|trans-title=Karanka will be the new sporting director of the national team|newspaper=Diario AS|first1=Ignacio|last1=Camacho|first2=Javier|last2=Martín|language=es|date=2 July 2025|access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Karanka's younger brother, [[David Karanka|David]], was also a footballer. A [[striker (association football)|striker]], he also appeared for Athletic Bilbao's first team but with much less impact, going on to spend the vast majority of his professional career in the second division or the lower leagues.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2002/05/20/mas_futbol/1021845623_850215.html|title=David Karanka desvela que Aitor puede volver a Bilbao|trans-title=David Karanka reveals Aitor may return to Bilbao|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=20 May 2002|access-date=13 November 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.laverdad.es/murcia/v/20111004/deportes_murcia/mas-futbol/anos-nada-20111004.html|title=33 años no son nada|trans-title=33 years is nothing|newspaper=[[La Verdad (Murcia)|La Verdad]]|first=José María|last=Pallarés Ripalda|language=es|date=4 October 2011|access-date=13 November 2013}}</ref>
